messages.subject: Simpson's lambda
parts:
Hi there,

In his paper, Simpson (1949) explains that “lambda can be simply interpreted as the probability that two individuals chosen at random and independently from the population will be found to belong to the same group”. Therefore, Lambda cannot represent genotypic diversity, but Simpson's complement index (1-lambda) can be interpreted as genotypic diversity, that is, the probability that two individuals chosen at random and independently from the population will belong to different groups. Is this correct? or maybe I am missing something?

Does poppr's lambda correspond to Simpson's index (the probability that two individuals belong to the same genotype) or Simpson's complement index (the probability that two individuals belong to different genotypes)?

Cheers
Niloofar

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Simpson's lambda
parts:
Hello Niloofar,

Poppr is calculating Simpson's complement index aka Simpson's Index of Diversity. 

Thank you for pointing this out on the group because it IS  an important distinction and has been brought up on the issue tracker: https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/issues/194#issuecomment-418705868 and I will update poppr's documentation to refer to "Simpson's complement index" in all the places lambda occurs to avoid confusion.

I hope that helps.

All the best,

Zhian
